analysis: The experiment strongly failed. Replacing the parent’s censored-watch BPR reward with a custom multi-target soft-label pointwise FM caused a large standalone validation drop: primary_mean 0.4786, delta -0.1273 versus incumbent, with paired CI95 [-0.1320, -0.1227] excluding zero across seeds. The degradation was broad rather than localized, appearing in every reported user-history, item-popularity, and tab slice, with larger harm for heavier-history users. This falsifies the core hypothesis that the blended soft supervision would be at least competitive standalone while offering useful diversity. Portfolio evidence also did not rescue it: challenger portfolio delta was -0.00025 with CI crossing zero, so there is no promotion case. The most supported interpretation is that the new target/loss changed the ranking in a harmful way—likely over-optimizing proxy engagement or losing pairwise/top-rank discrimination—rather than merely adding benign diversity.
next_lesson: Do not replace the proven pairwise censored-watch objective with a blended soft pointwise target; if reward shaping is revisited, keep long_view-centered pairwise ranking and test only a minimal auxiliary formulation.
